artifacts.summary: Research on wiring verify-deploy.sh into deploy-headless.sh: recommends a distinct new exit code and a --skip-slow verify-deploy.sh flag, and documents a real collision with skill-orchestrate's existing pre/post baseline redeploy checkpoint that this task's file_scope cannot itself fix.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's shell test suite gate (gate 8, tests/run-all.sh) dominates its wall-clock cost: measured 117.9s of a ~2.8min 12-gate total (~65-70%). When wiring verify-deploy.sh into a hot path (e.g. deploy-headless.sh), consider a gate-skip flag for the slow suite rather than always paying the full cost inline, especially if another caller (skill-orchestrate's inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint) already invokes the full script separately.

skill-orchestrate's Stage MT-3 step 7 inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint calls deploy-headless.sh and verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet as two SEPARATE calls (pre- and post-redeploy) specifically to baseline-diff findings and distinguish newly-introduced failures (defer) from pre-existing ones (proceed, branch c). Any future change that makes deploy-headless.sh itself hard-fail on verify-deploy findings must use a distinct exit code from deploy-headless.sh's existing exit 2 (nvim failure), so the orchestrator's checkpoint can eventually be taught to route that new failure mode through its existing baseline logic instead of its unconditional 'deploy-headless failed' branch (a), which would otherwise silently swallow branch (c)'s pre-existing-failure tolerance.
